Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Young woman with worsening severe lower central abdominal pain, associated light vaginal bleeding different from normal menstruation, nausea without vomiting, recent constipation now resolved, and use of Implanon contraceptive implant with irregular bleeding pattern. Allergy to amoxicillin noted. No fever or urinary symptoms.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with clinical presentation and DDx:  
  • Ectopic pregnancy (medium likelihood): Worsening lower abdominal pain with vaginal bleeding in reproductive age woman on contraception with a previous negative pregnancy test one month ago; requires urgent exclusion via pregnancy test and face-to-face examination.  
  • Pelvic inflammatory disease (medium likelihood): Abdominal pain with light vaginal bleeding and nausea; absence of fever and severe discharge weakens typical PID picture but cannot be excluded without exam and investigations.  
  • Ovarian torsion (medium likelihood): Severe worsening abdominal pain and nausea suggest possible torsion despite midline pain; urgent assessment needed.  
  • Constipation-related pain (low likelihood): Constipation noted but symptoms worsening despite resolution; vaginal bleeding unexplained by constipation.  
  • Side effects of Implanon (low likelihood): Commonly causes irregular bleeding but significant severe abdominal pain and nausea less typical, warranting further evaluation.  
- Working diagnosis: Undifferentiated lower abdominal pain with light vaginal bleeding in a woman with Implanon contraception; ectopic pregnancy cannot be excluded and requires urgent re-testing and clinical evaluation.  
- Management priorities: Urgent exclusion of ectopic pregnancy, clinical examination to identify or exclude surgical or infective causes; evaluate for pelvic inflammatory disease or adnexal pathology.  

Management Plan

- Arrange urgent face-to-face clinical abdominal examination at clinic for physical assessment and further diagnostic work-up.  
- Advise patient to complete pregnancy test as soon as possible today; if positive, contact service immediately for urgent assessment.  
- Educate patient to seek immediate care if symptoms worsen (increased pain, vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, fever, faintness).  
- Support line to assist in arranging clinic appointment.  
- No medications prescribed during this consultation; allergy to amoxicillin documented.  
- No explicit referral documented but prompt clinical review implied.  
- No other immediate investigations ordered, but subsequent investigations expected following physical exam.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Ectopic pregnancy (Medium likelihood)  
   - Justification: Constant worsening lower abdominal pain with vaginal bleeding different from period, sexual activity despite Implanon; previous negative pregnancy test one month ago does not exclude current pregnancy; urgent exclusion necessary.

2. Pelvic inflammatory disease (Medium likelihood)  
   - Justification: Abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, and nausea consistent with PID; absence of fever and severe discharge weakens but does not exclude diagnosis.

3. Ovarian torsion (Medium likelihood)  
   - Justification: Severe, worsening abdominal pain with nausea suggest torsion; midline location less typical but still plausible; urgent clinical exam required.
